newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money stable at 5.5/6.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money stable at 5.5/6.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was stable at 5.5/6.0 percent on Tuesday morning despite sustained ample liquidity, dealers said.
"Carry forward liquidity coupled with another fresh injection from the central bank this morning kept liquidity ample, but the rates remained generally stable," one dealer said.
Some 451 billion rupiah of central bank certificates (SBIs) were due today, with some 50 billion rupiah of SBIs for today settlement.
Dealers said weekly tax payments did not seem to have had much impact on the rupiah liquidity.
One- and three-month money were at 10.75/11.00 and 12.50/12.75 percent, respectively.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates stable. It offered seven-day SBIs at 6.5 percent, 14-day at 8.5 percent and one-month at 10.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 6.025 percent against 8.74 percent on Friday.
